To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the optical absorption of a plasmonic nanopatterned structure can be significantly improved, and that (2) the plasmonic enhancement can be further boosted by the introduction of a dielectric spacer between the plasmonic nanostructure and the light-harvester.

(1) the optical absorption of organic photovoltaics can be enhanced by the use of metallic nanoparticles and periodic metallic nanostructures, and (2) the optical absorption can be further improved by incorporating plasmonic nanostructure arrays with the use of a dielectric spacer layer.
the incorporation of plasmonic nanoparticles and nanostructured surfaces into OPV devices can enhance their power-conversion efficiencies (PCEs) by 20–30%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of organic solar cells that are capable of harvesting a significant fraction of the incident solar energy.
plasmonics for enhancing the light absorption and the charge collection efficiency in thin-film solar cells.
the development and optimization of organic photovoltaics and plasmonics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of plasmonic structures to increase light absorption in OPVs is still a promising approach, but the challenge is to achieve a high efficiency at the same time.

the use of metallic nanoparticles in OPV devices is a promising approach, but the use of periodic nanopatterned metal structures is more challenging due to the difficulties in the fabrication of such structures.
the incorporation of plasmonic nanoparticles in the active layer(s) of OPV devices can lead to a substantial improvement in device performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
plasmonic nanostructure-based light-trapping strategies are promising to improve the power conversion efficiencies of OPVs.
plasmonics has a great potential for OPVs, but the current state-of-the-art performance is still not comparable to that of conventional silicon-based solar cells.

the incorporation of plasmonic metallic nanoparticles in OPVs can enhance the light absorption of the active layer(s), but the enhancement is highly dependent on the size, shape, and location of the nanoparticles, and on the thickness of the active layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

plasmonic nanostructure-enhanced OPVs can be designed to improve the optical absorption of a thin-film organic light-harvesters, while maintaining a high open circuit voltage and low series resistance.
plasmonic nanostructure design is critical for the enhancement in optical absorption and power conversion efficiency of the OPVs.
plasmonically-enhanced OPV devices are still in their infancy, with the most promising results coming from periodic nanopatterned metal structures.
